domain: RT1062 core, boot, clock, debug and recovery
revision_note: REVISION 2. Revision 1 contained material errors caused by a stale pin read-back for U6-RTC part e3295. See superseded_findings. Every number below is re-derived from jobs/full-pin-harvest.results.json and cross-checked against the 14:58 GUI DRC.

drawing_oracle.self_test: SELF_TEST=OK, 13 battery cases including 4 RED, 3 FAIL-CLOSED, abstention and tolerance-guard controls
drawing_oracle.measures: do wires visually meet the pins they are labelled for

netlist_witness.measures: what EasyEDA's netlister binds, on the LIVE document
netlist_witness.used_as: independent witness, never to calibrate the geometry

instruments.separation_rule: Two distinct claims are kept apart throughout: 'the wire does not meet the pin in the drawing' (single-sheet-contract violation) and 'the pin is electrically unconnected' (netlist claim, which geometry alone cannot make on this host).

pin_data_provenance.reason: Diffing the two read-backs pin by pin: exactly ONE of 229 component parts moved between them - U6-RTC part e3295, by a uniform (+210, -170) across all 98 of its pins. Every other part is byte-identical. Revision 1 measured current wires against those stale coordinates for schematic rows A-G only, manufacturing 22 false floating-ball claims.

denominator.warning: FROZEN SNAPSHOT captured ~13:57, about one hour BEFORE the 14:58 DRC. The live document has moved past this hash. Every finding is a PROPOSAL for a single authorised writer to reconfirm.

coverage.note: U6-RTC is ONE multi-part component, not a duplicate: parts e3295 (rows A-G) and e3673 (rows H-P), 98 balls each, disjoint, union exactly 196 = the DVJ6B ball count. EasyEDA's own DRC confirms it as multi-part.

u6_floating_reconciliation.interpretation: The DRC's 80 is a strict SUBSET of the drawing oracle's 111, with ZERO DRC-only balls. Nothing the live netlister calls floating is drawn as connected in the frozen snapshot, which is the meaningful agreement. The 31 drawing-only balls all sit in part e3673 at 10-50 units from the nearest endpoint, and that endpoint always belongs to a NEIGHBOURING ball's stub, so they are not near-miss bindings. Leading explanation is the ~1 hour between the 13:57 freeze and the 14:58 DRC. UNRESOLVED until the source is re-frozen.

superseded_findings.revision_1_claim: Six of nine VDD_SOC_IN balls, seven of nineteen VSS balls, two NVCC_GPIO and two NVCC_EMC balls are unconnected
superseded_findings.truth: All of F6,F7,F8,F9,G6,G9 are on 1V15_CORE; A1,A14,B5,B10,E2,E13,G7 are on GND; E9,F10 on 3V3; E6,F5 on 3V3. Confirmed by both instruments.

superseded_findings.revision_1_claim: Boot straps and SWD terminate on orphan stubs ~210 units from their balls and never reach the processor; passive default is Boot-From-Fuses not Internal Boot
superseded_findings.truth: BOOT_MODE0 binds R10-RTC.1, R61-VAL.2 and U6-RTC.F11. BOOT_MODE1 binds R11-RTC.1 and U6-RTC.G14. SWD_SWDIO binds R16-RTDBG.1 and U6-RTC.E14. SWD_SWCLK binds R15-RTDBG.1 and U6-RTC.F12. Passive default IS BOOT_MODE[1:0]=10 = Internal Boot, as D13.1 requires. The '210 units' was the (+210,-170) stale offset itself - a uniform rigid translation across all 98 pins, which is the signature of a registration error, not a drawing error.

superseded_findings.revision_1_claim: JTAG_TDO (G13) is tied hard to GND against NXP guidance
superseded_findings.truth: G13 is FLOATING in both instruments. NXP's rule (fit no pull-up or pull-down on TDO) is SATISFIED as built. Reclassified INTENTIONAL_NC.

superseded_findings.revision_1_claim: Four GND stubs stop 5 units short of balls D4, D6, D9, D11
superseded_findings.truth: With correct coordinates the nearest endpoints are 10, 10, 70 and 50 units away and belong to other pins' stubs. These are four ordinary unused GPIO among the DRC's 80.

superseded_findings.revision_1_claim: S3_POR_REQ and RT_PWR_VALID are 5-unit near-misses at U9-ESP
superseded_findings.verdict: STILL TRUE OF THE FROZEN SNAPSHOT, WITHDRAWN AS A LIVE CLAIM
superseded_findings.truth: The drawing oracle confirms both wires meet no pin (90 and 100 units from U9-ESP, which is displaced by (5,-20) by the rejected-but-never-rolled-back canonical-esp-service-label-visibility-repair transaction). But the 14:58 DRC reports ZERO floating pins on the ESP32-S3, so the live document has been repaired. Not a live defect. Attribute to the S3 side, not the RT side.

superseded_findings.revision_1_claim: FLEXSPI_D2/D3 do not reach the processor, so quad-SPI XIP is impossible
superseded_findings.truth: Nets FLEXSPI_D2 and FLEXSPI_D3 bind only U8-RTDBG plus their pull-ups in the frozen snapshot, and U6-RTC P4/P5 carry no stub. But the DRC does NOT report P4/P5 floating, so the live netlist may already bind them. Re-freeze the source before acting.

authority_corrections.claim: rt_boot_mode0_pad GPIO_AD_B0_04 / rt_boot_mode1_pad GPIO_AD_B0_05, 100 kohm internal pull
authority_corrections.verdict: CONFIRMED CORRECT and stronger than stated: BOOT_MODE0/1 are not dedicated balls, they are the ALT0 reset-default function of those pads, on balls F11 and G14, each with a 100 kohm internal pull-DOWN (min 60k, max 140k).
authority_corrections.source: NXP IMXRT1060CEC Rev.4 Sec.5.1 Table 71 and Table 86; NXP MIMXRT105060HDUG Rev.4 Sec.6 Table 9 item 2

authority_corrections.claim: RT_RESET_REQ_N is carried by exactly ONE wire, is a genuine single-endpoint net, and is a K1E-016 violation
authority_corrections.verdict: WRONG. It is one wire (e66889, [[3065,4300],[3130,4300]]) but it has TWO endpoints landing exactly on SW1-RTC.2 and U7-RTC.3 (MR#). The drawing oracle's own single-pin-net list is BUCK_PG, ESP_UART0_RX, K1BR_IRQ_S3, K1BR_MISO_S3, K1BR_MOSI, MOTION_INT_S3, S3_POR_REQ - RT_RESET_REQ_N is not among them. The real defect on this net is RT-D01 and is of a different class.

authority_corrections.target: orchestrator message: 111 of 196 U6 balls unconnected
authority_corrections.claim: 111 unconnected, DRC agrees to the ball
authority_corrections.verdict: The 111 is the DRAWING-oracle number and it is reproducible. It is NOT the netlist number. The DRC says 80. The earlier 'agreement to the ball' was coincidental - my geometry then said 133, not 111.

taxonomy_note: Three dispositions are added beyond the brief's seven, because the brief has no bucket for 'ought to be connected and is not', nor for 'the two instruments disagree'. DEFECT_FLOATING and DEFECT_MISWIRED are real defects. DRAWING_GAP_NETLIST_OK is an explicit UNRESOLVED marker, not a pass and not a silent unknown.

C&K PTS645 terminals 1&2 are PERMANENTLY COMMON and 3&4 are PERMANENTLY COMMON; the momentary contact bridges {1,2} to {3,4}. The board wires pin1->GND and pin2->RT_RESET_REQ_N, i.e. across the always-closed pair, hard-shorting RT_RESET_REQ_N to GND. That holds U7-RTC MR# low permanently, so the supervisor asserts RESET# continuously and POR_B never releases. Repair: move RT_RESET_REQ_N to terminal 3 (optionally also 4->RT_RESET_REQ_N, 2->GND).
pins.source: C&K/Littelfuse PTS645 datasheet Rev CM.10/23/24 contact schematic; TI TPS3808 SBVS050M Table 6-1
